paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and spake again in parables unto them, saying,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν εἶπεν ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: Kai apokritheis ho Iēsous palin eipen en parabolais autois legōn·

paragraphs.text: The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a certain king, who made a marriage feast for his son,
paragraphs.original: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ, ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō basilei, hostis epoiēsen gamous tō hyiō autou.

paragraphs.text: and sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the marriage feast: and they would not come.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apesteilen tous doulous autou kalesai tous keklēmenous eis tous gamous, kai ouk ēthelon elthein.

paragraphs.text: Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them that are bidden, Behold, I have made ready my dinner; my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come to the marriage feast.
paragraphs.original: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων· Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ἡτοίμακα, οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα, καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα· δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
paragraphs.translit: palin apesteilen allous doulous legōn· Eipate tois keklēmenois· Idou to ariston mou hētoimaka, hoi tauroi mou kai ta sitista tethymena, kai panta hetoima· deute eis tous gamous.

paragraphs.text: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον, ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν, ὃς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de amelēsantes apēlthon, hos men eis ton idion agron, hos de epi tēn emporian autou·

paragraphs.text: and the rest laid hold on his servants, and treated them shamefully, and killed them.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de loipoi kratēsantes tous doulous autou hybrisan kai apekteinan.

paragraphs.text: But the king was wroth; and he sent his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὠργίσθη, καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de basileus ōrgisthē, kai pempsas ta strateumata autou apōlesen tous phoneis ekeinous kai tēn polin autōn eneprēsen.

paragraphs.text: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they that were bidden were not worthy.
paragraphs.original: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι·
paragraphs.translit: tote legei tois doulois autou· Ho men gamos hetoimos estin, hoi de keklēmenoi ouk ēsan axioi·

paragraphs.text: Go ye therefore unto the partings of the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage feast.
paragraphs.original: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, καὶ ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
paragraphs.translit: poreuesthe oun epi tas diexodous tōn hodōn, kai hosous ean heurēte kalesate eis tous gamous.

paragraphs.text: And those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was filled with guests.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας οὓς εὗρον, πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς· καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthontes hoi douloi ekeinoi eis tas hodous synēgagon pantas hous heuron, ponērous te kai agathous· kai eplēsthē ho gamos anakeimenōn.

paragraphs.text: But when the king came in to behold the guests, he saw there a man who had not on a wedding-garment:
paragraphs.original: εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου·
paragraphs.translit: eiselthōn de ho basileus theasasthai tous anakeimenous eiden ekei anthrōpon ouk endedymenon endyma gamou·

paragraphs.text: and he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding-garment? And he was speechless.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου; ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autō· Hetaire, pōs eisēlthes hōde mē echōn endyma gamou; ho de ephimōthē.

paragraphs.text: Then the king said to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and cast him out into the outer darkness; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
paragraphs.original: τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τοῖς διακόνοις· Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: tote ho basileus eipen tois diakonois· Dēsantes autou podas kai cheiras ekbalete auton eis to skotos to exōteron· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.

paragraphs.text: For many are called, but few chosen.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.
paragraphs.translit: polloi gar eisin klētoi oligoi de eklektoi.

paragraphs.text: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might ensnare him in [his] talk.
paragraphs.original: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Tote poreuthentes hoi Pharisaioi symboulion elabon hopōs auton pagideusōsin en logō.

paragraphs.text: And they send to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, and carest not for any one: for thou regardest not the person of men.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·
paragraphs.translit: kai apostellousin autō tous mathētas autōn meta tōn Hērōdianōn legontes· Didaskale, oidamen hoti alēthēs ei kai tēn hodon tou theou en alētheia didaskeis, kai ou melei soi peri oudenos, ou gar blepeis eis prosōpon anthrōpōn·

paragraphs.text: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
paragraphs.original: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;
paragraphs.translit: eipon oun hēmin ti soi dokei· exestin dounai kēnson Kaisari ē ou;

paragraphs.text: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why make ye trial of me, ye hypocrites?
paragraphs.original: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Τί με πειράζετε, ὑποκριταί;
paragraphs.translit: gnous de ho Iēsous tēn ponērian autōn eipen· Ti me peirazete, hypokritai;

paragraphs.text: Show me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a denarius.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου. οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον.
paragraphs.translit: epideixate moi to nomisma tou kēnsou. hoi de prosēnenkan autō dēnarion.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Tinos hē eikōn hautē kai hē epigraphē;

paragraphs.text: They say unto him, Caesar`s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things that are Caesar`s; and unto God the things that are God`s.
paragraphs.original: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος. τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō· Kaisaros. tote legei autois· Apodote oun ta Kaisaros Kaisari kai ta tou theou tō theō.

paragraphs.text: And when they heard it, they marvelled, and left him, and went away.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν, καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousantes ethaumasan, kai aphentes auton apēlthan.

paragraphs.text: On that day there came to him Sadducees, they that say that there is no resurrection: and they asked him,
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι, λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν, καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
paragraphs.translit: En ekeinē tē hēmera prosēlthon autō Saddoukaioi, legontes mē einai anastasin, kai epērōtēsan auton

paragraphs.text: saying, Teacher, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα, ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Didaskale, Mōysēs eipen· Ean tis apothanē mē echōn tekna, epigambreusei ho adelphos autou tēn gynaika autou kai anastēsei sperma tō adelphō autou.

paragraphs.text: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first married and deceased, and having no seed left his wife unto his brother;
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δὲ παρʼ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν, καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de parʼ hēmin hepta adelphoi· kai ho prōtos gēmas eteleutēsen, kai mē echōn sperma aphēken tēn gynaika autou tō adelphō autou·

paragraphs.text: in like manner the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος, ἕως τῶν ἑπτά·
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs kai ho deuteros kai ho tritos, heōs tōn hepta·

paragraphs.text: And after them all, the woman died.
paragraphs.original: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἡ γυνή.
paragraphs.translit: hysteron de pantōn apethanen hē gynē.

paragraphs.text: In the resurrection therefore whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οὖν τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή; πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: en tē anastasei oun tinos tōn hepta estai gynē; pantes gar eschon autēn.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.
paragraphs.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen autois· Planasthe mē eidotes tas graphas mēde tēn dynamin tou theou·

paragraphs.text: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as angels in heaven.
paragraphs.original: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἄγγελοι θεοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν·
paragraphs.translit: en gar tē anastasei oute gamousin oute gamizontai, allʼ hōs angeloi theou en tō ouranō eisin·

paragraphs.text: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,
paragraphs.original: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγοντος·
paragraphs.translit: peri de tēs anastaseōs tōn nekrōn ouk anegnōte to rhēthen hymin hypo tou theou legontos·

paragraphs.text: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not [the God] of the dead, but of the living.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ; οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων.
paragraphs.translit: Egō eimi ho theos Abraam kai ho theos Isaak kai ho theos Iakōb; ouk estin ho theos nekrōn alla zōntōn.

paragraphs.text: And when the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousantes hoi ochloi exeplēssonto epi tē didachē autou.

paragraphs.text: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, gathered themselves together.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi de Pharisaioi akousantes hoti ephimōsen tous Saddoukaious synēchthēsan epi to auto.

paragraphs.text: And one of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, trying him:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtēsen heis ex autōn nomikos peirazōn auton·

paragraphs.text: Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?
paragraphs.original: Διδάσκαλε, ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ;
paragraphs.translit: Didaskale, poia entolē megalē en tō nomō;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου·
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē autō· Agapēseis kyrion ton theon sou en holē tē kardia sou kai en holē tē psychē sou kai en holē tē dianoia sou·

paragraphs.text: This is the great and first commandment.
paragraphs.original: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη ἐντολή.
paragraphs.translit: hautē estin hē megalē kai prōtē entolē.

paragraphs.text: And a second like [unto it] is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
paragraphs.original: Δευτέρα δὲ ὁμοία αὐτῇ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Deutera de homoia autē· Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton.

paragraphs.text: On these two commandments the whole law hangeth, and the prophets.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
paragraphs.translit: en tautais tais dysin entolais holos ho nomos krematai kai hoi prophētai.

paragraphs.text: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,
paragraphs.original: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς
paragraphs.translit: Synēgmenōn de tōn Pharisaiōn epērōtēsen autous ho Iēsous

paragraphs.text: saying, What think ye of the Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, [The son] of David.
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ; τίνος υἱός ἐστιν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τοῦ Δαυίδ.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Ti hymin dokei peri tou christou; tinos hyios estin; legousin autō· Tou Dauid.

paragraphs.text: He saith unto them, How then doth David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πῶς οὖν Δαυὶδ ἐν πνεύματι καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: legei autois· Pōs oun Dauid en pneumati kalei auton kyrion legōn·

paragraphs.text: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Till I put thine enemies underneath thy feet?
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου;
paragraphs.translit: Eipen kyrios tō kyriō mou· Kathou ek dexiōn mou heōs an thō tous echthrous sou hypokatō tōn podōn sou;

paragraphs.text: If David then calleth him Lord, how is he his son?
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν Δαυὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον, πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν;
paragraphs.translit: ei oun Dauid kalei auton kyrion, pōs hyios autou estin;

paragraphs.text: And no one was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ λόγον, οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπʼ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι.
paragraphs.translit: kai oudeis edynato apokrithēnai autō logon, oude etolmēsen tis apʼ ekeinēs tēs hēmeras eperōtēsai auton ouketi.
